A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same VERA framework and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Relocated experiments and limitations can be matched reliably.

before.justification: V1 reports original UCF-Crime and XD-Violence results, ablations, transfer experiments and qualitative analyses in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: V2 retains those original empirical results and additionally reports a qualitative caption comparison with LAVAD in Figure 6.

M1.justification: The frozen-VLM learner/optimizer procedure, guiding questions and three-stage inference pipeline remain unchanged. Section 3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same operations; shortened explanations do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate UCF-Crime and XD-Violence, including the same traffic/store subsets and qualitative videos. The added caption comparison reuses scenes from the existing Arrest007_x264 example.

E2.justification: V2 adds LAVAD as a direct caption comparator in Section 4.4 and Figure 6, where v1 illustrated VERA alone. LAVAD already participated in numerical comparisons, whose comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: The benchmark protocols retain the 10% validation holdout, AUC/AP metrics, model configurations, sampling, training budget and inference hyperparameters. The added caption comparison uses existing scenes without documenting different experimental settings.

E4.justification: Figure 6 adds a qualitative analysis comparing captions for three scenes. Existing ablations, transfer tests and sensitivity analyses are retained; the batch-size/frame-count study moves from v1 Section 4.3 and Table 5 to v2 Appendix B.3 and Table 12.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Point-estimate reporting and the moving-average presentation of validation accuracy remain unchanged.

E6.justification: Matched numerical results are unchanged, including VERA's 86.55% UCF-Crime AUC, 88.26% XD-Violence AUC and 70.54% XD-Violence AP. V2 Figure 6 newly reports three LAVAD captions alongside VERA's existing responses.

T1.justification: The task definitions, sampling formulation, Equations (1)-(5), similarity weighting and Gaussian scoring definitions are retained. Neither version adds or revises theoretical results or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contributions and conclusion retain the same claims about adapting frozen VLMs through learned questions, avoiding instruction tuning and external reasoning modules, and achieving effective, transferable explainable anomaly detection.

C2.justification: V2 Section 4.4 attributes the contrast between VERA's descriptive reasoning and LAVAD's plain captions to the learned guiding questions. Existing transfer interpretations and AP qualifications remain. The visual-encoder limitation moves from Section 5 to Appendix C without substantive expansion.

D1.justification: V2 omits the explicit NVIDIA RTX A6000 disclosure and several dataset-size details, including training-set sizes and test-frame totals. Prompt templates, pseudocode, principal hyperparameters and the project URL remain. These omissions do not establish changed hardware or data.

R1.justification: V2 adds HAWK and VADCLIP citations in Section 2. Condensing the baseline background removes references for I3D, C3D, VideoSwin, ResNet and ResNeXt. The central positioning relative to VML, TextGrad and explainable VAD remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 condenses experimental background, abbreviates verbalized learning as VL, shortens method headings and reorganizes the qualitative discussion. It moves the batch-size analysis and limitations into Appendices B.3 and C and adds author contact details; the main narrative remains largely intact.

P2.justification: V2 adds the caption-comparison Figure 6, recolors Figure 2 and reduces Figure 5 to one column while presenting its guiding questions in prose. The batch-size table and several appendix figures are relocated; existing plots and table structures are largely retained.

improvement.justification: The new side-by-side caption comparison in Figure 6 makes the claimed explanation differences directly inspectable, modestly strengthening the paper's exposition while preserving its quantitative evidence. This limited gain is tempered by the removed GPU disclosure and reduced readability of the smaller Figure 5.
